title: I spent 6 weeks in Godot going DEEP on water (excuse the pun!)
author: stankuslee
selftext:
This is for my game *Portolan* \- a 'serious' take on *Sid Meier's Pirates!* with historically accurate in-game economy and trading, politics and combat in a to-scale Caribbean. 

All built in Godot using Forward+. This is NOT a one shot prompt 'Claude made this in 3 hours" type post. It's the result of a lot of iteration.

Swell, wind speed etc are all configurable.

I'm very proud of what I've created, and wanted to share.

LMK if you have questions about the stack, the process, or anything else.

comments.body: Ok what's the stack and process xD

replies.author: stankuslee
replies.body:
The stack is Godot, GDScript for coordination, and GLSL compute shaders for the wave simulation and foam, with a separate water-rendering shader.

The process is very iterative: capture footage, watch it closely, compare it with real water, then check the simulation data to understand what’s causing anything that looks wrong. Adjust, rerun the same views and compare again. Lots of small cycles based on observed behaviour... especially how foam forms and fades, waves meet the shore, and water contacts the boat, which i am working on now.
